Situation
sit-u-AY-shun
n. (position; the place where a thing is set)
Latin situs, a site or position. In the Authorized Version the word is never about circumstances in the modern sense; it means literal position on the ground — where a city sits, and how it sits.

Biblical Definition

The men of Jericho bring Elisha a problem that is exactly a matter of position: “Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water is naught, and the ground barren” (2 Kings 2:19). Everything about the site was right except the one thing that makes a site habitable, and the prophet healed the spring with salt in a new cruse, saying the LORD had healed these waters. The other use is the loftiest description of Jerusalem in the Psalms: “Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:2). The beauty named there is not architecture but placement — where God set the city. Scripture thus uses the word for something a city cannot choose about itself and cannot change: the position given it. Zion's glory is that the great King chose to set his house there.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines situation as position; seat; location; and the place where a thing is set with respect to surrounding objects.

expand to see more

SITUATION, n. Position; seat; location in respect to something else; as, the situation of a city on a river.

SITUATION, n. State; condition; as, a man in easy or embarrassed situation.

SITUATION, n. Place; office; as, a situation under the government.

SITE, n. Situation; local position; as the site of a city or of a house.

PLEASANT, a. Pleasing; agreeable; grateful to the mind or to the senses.

Key Scripture

2 Kings 2:19 — "And the men of the city said unto Elisha, Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water is naught, and the ground barren."

2 Kings 2:21 — "And he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus saith the LORD, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land."

Psalm 48:2 — "Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King."

Psalm 48:1 — "A Song and Psalm for the sons of Korah. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness."

Modern Corruption

The word has shifted from position given to circumstances suffered, and with it the modern habit of explaining a man wholly by his situation; Scripture uses it of a place God appointed, and of a bad spring God healed.

expand to see more

In current speech a person's situation explains him: he is a product of where he finds himself, and both his conduct and his prospects are read off his circumstances. The KJV never uses the word that way. A situation is a position, and in both occurrences it is a position assigned rather than achieved. Zion is beautiful for situation because God set his city there; Jericho's situation was pleasant because the site was good. What is wrong at Jericho is not the situation but the water, and the remedy is not relocation but healing.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition of the word itself. The principle to recover is providential placement. The Athenians were told that God determined the times before appointed and the bounds of men's habitation, and Paul told the Corinthians that as God hath distributed to every man, so let him walk. A believer's situation — his country, his family, his century, his employment — is a station given him to be faithful in, not an accident to be escaped before obedience can begin. And where the ground is barren and the water naught, the God of 2 Kings 2 still heals springs.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew mowshab (H4186), a seat or dwelling-place; nowph (H5131), elevation, beautiful for situation; qiryah (H7151), a city; ra (H7451), bad or naught.

expand to see more

Hebrew mowshab (H4186) — a seat, a site, a dwelling; the situation of the city in 2 Kings 2:19.

Hebrew nowph (H5131) — elevation, height; beautiful for situation in Psalm 48:2.

Hebrew ra (H7451) — bad, evil, naught; the water that spoiled a pleasant site.

Hebrew rapha (H7495) — to heal, to mend; what the LORD did to the waters of Jericho.

Hebrew Tsiyown (H6726) — Zion; the city of the great King, glorious in its placement.

Usage

"“The situation of this city is pleasant... but the water is naught” — the one flaw."

"“Beautiful for situation... is mount Zion” — glory in where God set it."

"“The city of the great King” — what makes a situation glorious."
